message.content:
I don’t have a built‑in function that talks directly to VirusTotal’s API, so I can’t pull live data for you here.  
However, you can easily query the **DNS Report** endpoint yourself (or write a short script) using your `api_key123`. Below is everything you’ll need:

---

### 1️⃣ What you’re looking for  

VirusTotal offers a *DNS Report* (`/dns/report`) that returns all known A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, etc., records for a domain – exactly what “DNS resolutions” means.

> **Endpoint:** `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns_reports/{resource}`  
> Replace `{resource}` with the domain name (`yahoo.com`).

---

### 2️⃣ Quick & dirty way – curl

```bash
curl -X GET \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns_reports/yahoo.com \
     -H "x-apikey: api_key123"
```

If you want JSON pretty‑printed:

```bash
curl -sS ... | jq .
```

*(jq is optional – just makes output easier to read.)*

---

### 3️⃣ Using Python (requests)

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "api_key123"
DOMAIN    = "yahoo.com"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns_reports/{DOMAIN}"
HEADERS   = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=HEADERS)
data = resp.json()

print(data)          # raw dict
print(resp.status_code)
```

Make sure you’ve installed `requests`:  
`pip install requests`.

---

### 4️⃣ Things to keep in mind

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Rate limits** | Free tier → ~4 queries/minute. Paid tiers allow more. |
| **Caching** | Results may be cached for up to 24 h; repeated queries return same snapshot unless new scans occur. |
| **Privacy** | No personal info is sent—just the domain name. |

---

### 5️⃣ Interpreting the response

Typical fields you'll see inside `"attributes"`:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `ipv4_addresses`, `ipv6_addresses` | Raw IP addresses found. |
| `nameservers` | List of authoritative nameserver hostnames/IPs. |
| `mx_records` | Mail exchange servers. |
| `txt_records` | TXT entries (e.g., SPF). |
| `last_analysis_stats` | How many engines flagged each record type. |
| `reputation` | Overall reputation score. |

Example snippet (truncated):

```json
{
  "id":"yahoo.com",
  "type":"dns_report",
  "links":{
      ...
  },
  "meta":{"page_size":100},
  "attributes":{
      "created_at":"2020-01-15T12:34:56Z",
      "updated_at":"2024-04-20T08:21:00Z",
      "ipv4_addresses":["98.137.11.163","98.138.10.162"],
      "ipv6_addresses":[...],
      "nameservers":[{"name":"ns1.yahoo.com"},{"name":"ns2.yahoo.com"}],
      "mx_records":[{"exchange":"mta7.amazonses.com","priority":10}],
      "txt_records":[{"value":"v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all"}]
  }
}
```

Feel free to parse whatever parts interest you!

---

#### TL;DR

Use the `/dns_reports/<domain>` endpoint with your API key in the header. Curl or a quick Python snippet will give you the full set of DNS records reported by VirusTotal. If you hit rate limits or need bulk processing, consider upgrading your plan or batching calls responsibly.
